As a Member of Congress, I will be voting no on the House GOP Reproductive Health Care Surveillance Act, and as a doctor I urge all my colleagues to oppose this bill.

No one, especially politicians, has the right to tell a me how to tend to my patients. https://t.co/wfVKdn4gSz

Thank you to @AmerMedicalAssn for giving me the opportunity to speak at the #AMANAC. 

I will continue to work in Congress to strengthen and protect Medicare.

Patients deserve to have access to physicians. Period. https://t.co/RUkOmpiE0V

The American people: We want lower prices!

Republicans: We’re actually going to raise prices by getting into a trade war. But it’s all worth it because then we’ll be able to support the President’s policies to cut Medicaid, SNAP, and Social Security. We are so back!

Republicans have made one thing clear: they want to cut Medicaid.

They’ll deny it, but actions speak louder than words, and Republicans have already taken steps to slash Medicaid.

Democrats will fight back.

I was curious how Republicans would spin their Medicaid cuts, and it’s just as ridiculous as I expected.

When they say "reforms" to Medicaid, they mean cuts.

Reforms = Cuts.

Honored to be named a top healthcare leader in NJ by @INSIDER__NJ (glad to share the title with @FrankPallone !).

As a physician & member of the Congressional Doctors Caucus, I’ll keep fighting for patients, providers & better care. https://t.co/bcsyOokZVd

$1.5 trillion in cuts all but guarantees devastating blows to Medicaid, Social Security, and SNAP.

These might not be “essential” to the billionaires @SpeakerJohnson is catering to — but to everyday Americans, they’re critical.

I worked at VA hospitals. The system isn’t perfect, but it’s the backbone of our promise to veterans—and it delivers better outcomes for them than anywhere else.

Trump’s admin betrayed that promise: cutting VA staff, slashing mental health care, and firing more veterans than ever before.

We must protect veterans’ benefits. No exceptions.

Today is Medicaid Matters Day of Action. I visited VNACJ Community Health Center & discussed the importance of Medicaid in providing cost-effective and affordable care to patients.

106,643 people in our district rely on Medicaid. The current Republican budget proposal would rip billions of dollars away from Medicaid in order to fund tax cuts for their billionaire friends. 

We can't let these cuts go through--lives depend on it.

I don’t know any doctor who would think it was a good idea to take away food and healthcare for children.

Preventative care is the most cost-efficient form of healthcare. And when it comes to our young people, investing in their health now saves government dollars down the line. 

This is not efficiency. Who does this benefit?

2. They’ve stalled cancer breakthroughs.

There was a major breakthrough for colon cancer treatment, but now it’s on hold thanks to government layoffs. Clinical trials are delayed, even for patients already enrolled.

(Reminder: 1 in 4 Americans will face colon cancer.)

Today I proposed an amendment to guarantee that veterans who depend on Medicaid don’t lose coverage. 

Every single Republican voted against it. 
 
Unlike my Republican colleagues, I am willing to keep our country’s promises to those who served. https://t.co/GYxP0XuDaT

I don’t know any doctors who would say taking away someone’s healthcare was a good idea. Yet Republican have proposed $880 billion in Medicaid cuts in order to fund tax breaks for the 1%. 

I stood alongside my fellow Dem Doctors in Congress to protest these cuts and defend Medicaid.

As both a Congressman and a doctor, it is clear to me just how devastating cuts to Medicaid would be for millions of Americans.

Read my Op-Ed below:
https://t.co/HlAchNYnWn

I asked VA Secretary Collins if he would protect the veterans who will lose their health care if Republicans’ gut Medicaid. 

His response? He said he “doesn’t foresee that happening.” A ludicrous thing to say when Republicans voted for billions in Medicaid cuts just last night in committee. 

Roughly 1 in 10 veterans rely on Medicaid as their primary form of healthcare. Sec. Collins, what are you going to do to protect them?

House Republicans just passed one of the most destructive bills in recent memory—gutting Medicaid and SNAP. 

It’s pure cruelty, showing who they really care about: billionaires. 

This is a dark day for everyday Americans—and for our democracy.

American people: We want affordable health care and food on our tables. 

Republicans: https://t.co/HX7BIADUbK
Wild that @SpeakerJohnson is 'very disappointed' that Elon hates the bill—but not at all concerned that 304,000 of his own constituents could lose their health care if it becomes law.

It’s official. The CBO is the *non-partisan* office that estimates how much things cost, and they see what we see: Millions of people will lose their health care, all to pay for tax cuts for billionaires.

Jokes about Elon and Trump aside, we’re witnessing the world’s two most powerful people argue while our government cuts basic services and looks to kick millions of people off of their healthcare. 

The American people deserve better. https://t.co/wCF9UOkGQG

1. Women have died after having miscarriages because doctors were forced to delay procedures that would have been considered an abortion. 

Doctors have also reported needing to delay necessary care until patients were at risk of death or permanent injury.
4. Over half of physicians in states with abortion bans considered leaving their states, and 1 in 10 actually did move since Dobbs. Pregnant patients will suffer with no access to obstetric care.

Your rights, your sister’s rights, your daughter’s rights, or your wife’s rights and health should not depend on where in the country you live. 

All of this is preventable. It’s time to get the government out of the doctor’s office.

To call this bad is an understatement. This could be deadly for millions of children. 
 
There's a reason we don't hear about kids getting Hepatitis anymore: we have vaccines that prevent them from getting it. RFK now wants to undo that.
 
The U.S. needs to take health recommendations from doctors and scientists, not conspiracy theorists.

Health care decisions should be between a doctor and their patient. Period.

This decision continues to put women’s access to reproductive health care at serious risk.

There is no room for politics in the exam room.
